title: MTC Day 1
body:
MTC Day 1

Got to the MTC today, got the tour and unpacked. It’s a little hectic now, but I can tell it will be good once classes start and I get used to the schedule.

The flight here was good. There were 16 of us – 12 elders, 4 sisters. I sat next to Elder Mckee on the plane; He also is my MTC comp – cool. He’s tall and from Utah, seems like a real nice guy. Had lunch an hour ago – all you can eat baby! About to go to my first meeting. I’m really excited. All the guys seem nice and willing to help. I think I will learn quickly.

body: I find it amazing how the Lord can work good, even through all of our mortal weaknesses, pride, and mistakes. Like how it took me 2 years longer than it should have to get here on my mission, but the spirit bears witness that it is God’s plan that I’m here with all my brothers here with me. Truly God is all knowing and His love infinite. And when the two combine, it is the miracles we see in our lives; it is the miracle of our lives. “God is our heavenly father; He wants us to be happy and loves us;” for this reason I’m here; and this love I hope to help others discover, and continue to discover myself. It is this Love that He wants us to have with Him for Eternity; It is this Love which is life eternal.

body: We went contacting today. It seems like a dream already. I was more shy than I thought I’d be, I’ll do better next time. But it was intimidating and truly humbling. I could speak ok, but I could not understand very well. But me and Elder McKee gave out all 7 Book of Mormon’s that we took, so that was really good. It was my first taste of truly being a brasilian missionary. Then, Irmão Gonçalves gave an amazing lesson on recognizing the Spirit. First, always be trying to invite the Spirit; focus always on the mission. Then remember to give God credit for all of our good thoughts and ideas, because that is feeling the spirit. All things good are promptings from the spirit. It’s simple, but hard to be that humble. What a good thought. I thank God that He inspired Irmão Gonçalves to inspire me. I love feeling the Holy Ghost and am glad to be able to recognize it more in my life.

body: Just got back from my second proselyting trip. It was amazing. So much better than last time. It was easier to talk and understand (although it was still hard to understand, we did good). I really felt like we were led by the Spirit and found people who will read it. One guy was familiar w/ the BoM because his ex-wife had one, so that might work out good. The best contact though was a muslim. He didn’t accept the BoM at first so we asked him why and he explained how nobody knows which church is true. Then I taught Him about the Apostasy and the First Vision, had him read Moroni’s promise and testified. He was touched and promised us that he would read it. It was amazing! Never thought I’d give a BoM to a Muslim. He seemed really interested after we taught him. I felt really good about it. I love being a missionary.

body: Holy Smokes! I forgot to write yesterday. Sorry! Had a good lesson today by Gonçalves, about loving God. And if we truly love God we would keep His commandments perfectly. Gonçalves gave the extreme that you either love God or you hate Him. Of course, perfection is something that takes work to achieve, and we can love Him in that process. But the point is valid. There are a lot of selfish tendencies deep inside me that need to be driven out. I desire God to help me consecrate my existence to Him, but it’s such a hard task to accomplish. I need to pray to know how to balance my personal life goals and desires with His plan for me. I need to discover his plan for me. I need to learn how to utilize my talents in a way that can align our interests or desires. I pray the mission makes me who He wants me to be.

Messages from Missionaries

Elder Dylan Payton Thomas Cleghorn, What up Elder? Well our time at the CTM is up and our time as comps has been fun. Keep to the Faith. Hold on the rod. I know the Truth is true. I know you do too. I’ll see you in Campinas Brother! Elder McKee

Elder Cleghorn (Derick) It’s crazy how fast time flys. I’m really glad that we are going to the same mission so that we can still see eachother and hang out. When the times get hard all you have to do is kneel down and pray and I promise that you will instantly feel better. Just keep the faith and represent the name on your badge. Elder Johnson

Elder Cleghorn. “A palavra é uma flecha, se lançada com o intuito de salvar uma alma, pode atingir o coração.” Te amo cara, você é uma grande pessoa e será um grande Missionário. Me envie fotos. “Elder Harrington”

Elder Cleghorn, It’s been awesome to get to know you here at the CTM! I know that coming on a mission was a struggle for you and so I really respect your decision to come out here. Thank you so much for the spirit you have added to our room! I have greatly appreciated your reverance for the gospel. We have had some awesome discussions! Keep up the good work. I’m sure we’ll see eachother novamente which is good. But until then, “God be with you”. Elder Gardner

Elder Cleghorn, Wow, can you believe how fast 9 weeks has gone by? It has been Amazing hasn’t it? Everybody in our District has been so Amazing. We have All grown together so much & it has been just Absolutely Awesome. I shall never forget your conversion story you told at the Beginning of our stay. You truly inspired me to know for myself the Truthfulness of the Book of Mormon. Thank You! Keep the Faith my Celtic Brother & for sure stay in Touch! God Bless! With Love, Elder Bryant McKnight

Elder D. Cleghorn, I will never forget you man! You are such a funny guy! You really showed me how to be obedient, patient, and humble and still have fun! I’m glad that you really started to open up in these last few weeks. You have a great knowledge of the gospel and I am so grateful for the opportunity I have had to get to know you! You have a great testimony that will inspire alot of people! Stay strong, Keep the Faith! Eu amo você! Elder Preston Guthrie

body: Today was good. I felt the Spirit alot. We watched Finding Faith in Christ with a family, what a powerful film! Also, I had a bit of a revelation about how the Atonement is infinite; because it’s happening now. All points of time passed before Christ in that moment, so as we live and use our agency, we literally are deciding what sins he will pay for. So, when he says if you love me, keep my commands, he’s saying if you love me don’t commit the sin that will cause me to suffer – because the atonement is still happening now – even though the physical suffering occured in a single moment. It’s eternal because it’s not bound by time, is happening, was happening, yet all passed before Him in an instant. It’s hard to explain in writing but it’s cool to understand better. The best way I can think to say it simply is that “It’s still happening then.” That’s how it’s eternal. I’m grateful to be receiving more light and truth as I grow.

Then when we arrived I felt the Spirit guide the lesson. At the start, I just wanted to invite everyone to go to church. But then Consuelo started talking about since the baptism she has had a peace in her life, so I shared João 14:26 and testified about the Gift of the Holy Ghost. Then she shared that at her baptism her mom came to her mind, which was weird because her mom passed away 22 years ago and it’s been a while since she thought about her mom. Then I testified that it was a vision from God. That her mom had been waiting for this moment and is rejoicing on the other side of the veil. As I said this I felt a strong confirmation that it was, indeed, true. It’s amazing to have such an experience with the Holy Ghost. The Spirit World exists and their work needs to be done; they’re waiting. I know this now.

body: 2 days ago I had a really good experience; a miracle. We went to teach Marcos, a contact we made 12 October. But alas, we did not find his house, so we figured that he lied to us and went and taught our other lessons. I was with Edinaldo and Elder Pacheco and Elder Garcia had gone way over to the bairro of Silvia. We had planned that they would catch the bus there and I would hop on as it passes the chapel – so they don’t have to get off and pay for another bus. So I was sitting in front of the Church waiting for the bus when Marcos appears wanting to be taught. At that same moment I received the call that the other Elders had entered the bus. So we went in to the chapel and I taught him the fastest Restoration lesson of my life: 5 minutes. And he accepted baptism! As I was trying to close the lesson I got the call that the bus was passing in front of the church! So I said “sorry, but I have to go!” And ran out the door and left Edinaldo to wrap it up. The bus was already at the bus stop so I ran as fast as I could, waving my arms, and barely caught it, in the knick of time. It was a really cool experience for me and I’m glad the Lord helped it all come together.

title: Journal entry
body:
Yesterday night I was laying in bed, waiting to sleep, and I received some revelations; I also learned how to better receive such inspiration through virtue and constant pondering. The first revelation was a confirmation of the exhortation of my Patriarchal Blessing to continue to prepare myself for my life’s responsibilities through education and service. I was pondering about the Liahona and the Apostles. They have to give talks every conference and often write articles for the Liahona. And it struck me, you really have to prepare yourself to given amounts of trust in God’s kingdom here on Earth. Education will help me have a wealth (D&C 84:85) of knowledge, a database the Holy Ghost can access. And constant service is how to apply the knowledge I’ve gained and an opportunity to gain experience and further develop the attributes of Christ.

As I realized how amazing it was to receive revelation, I received some insight to Light. Just like how we’re blind without physical light, our mind’s eye needs spiritual light to see visions and receive revelations. To ponder is to open the mind’s eye. This removes darkness from the mind. (D&C 88:67)

Virtue is the ability to constantly ponder like this to receive such light.

title: Journal entry
body:
I have a few entrys to write from the past few days:

We watched “The Restoration” with Sueli and Patricia and I was filled w/ the Spirit. It is amazing how the Spirit has such an amazing power to sanctify.

I learned how light and truth work with the minds eye to enlighten the soul. I’ll try and describe this revelation but I know it’ll be difficult. We know that light is gained thru obedience and lost thru disobedience. This allows the minds eye to open and close. When we sin, our mind (our ability to ponder and perceive; especially on spiritual subjects) becomes foggy. It seems to me that this is the veil. Under the principles of righteousness our VISION is enhanced, our mind opens w/ LIGHT. The veil is thinned. And thus, revelation is more easily obtained. I think that this is inseperably connected w/ the presence of the Holy Ghost.

Memorizing Scriptures truly sparks revelation and inspiration.

We had a lesson with Fernanda. She remarked her baptism for next week, which I think is fine. She’s been going to church for 3 years and finally is planning the date – and for the right reasons, too. She told us about a sacred experience she had. When she was about 6 years old, she dreamed about her Mom (who had passed away) in a place – a house – that made a deep impression in her mind and heart. But she never dreamed such a dream again. Recently, when she prayed to know if the Book of Mormon is true, she had the dream of that same house. She told us this crying, because she knew that God used this to answer her prayer, that He was communicating that her and her Mom could be together again after this life.

It’s truly amazing to me how the Lord answers our prayers in a way that is perfect for us, individually. What a blessing it is to serve a mission, to see how GREAT the Lord’s hand is. The Church really is true, because He tells us so.

title: Journal entry
body:
Feliz Natal!!! So there is another journal entry I need to add that I wrote on another piece of paper. But for now I’ll just describe what happened yesterday.

First of all, we made lunch in the office. I did the rice and strogonoff, which turned out really good. I’m really proud of myself. Afterwards we all (7 of us) put on Santa hats and hit the streets singing and giving away gift packages we put together.

As we were passing a bar everyone cheered at us – there were a good 70 people at this bar. So we went over to them and sang. Afterwards they yelled louder than a rock show for us. Haha it was great!

Then as we were walking down the street a car passes us. And the guy said “hey are you the ones that were singing? I’m going to a party to be Santa, you guys wanna go with me and leave a message and sing?” So we jumped in the car with him and did the gig. It was in a closed condominium and only had eleitos there. We found about 5 families. It truly was a miracle and a fulfilling of our President’s promise. Later today I’ll speak with my folks. That’ll be nice. I pray that today will have great miracles also. God is Good.

title: Journal entry
body:
Wow a New Year! It blows my mind that 9 months have flown by already. Being called Secretary certainly wasn’t what I expected here in the mission, but it has been a blessing. Working in Castelo w/ the assistants (Elder Greener & Elder Clares) is a blessing. We’re on fire. The Lord is sending so many miracles our way. Our goal for January is 22 baptisms – we’ve already marked 24! It’s amazing. I know we’ll have to mark alot more to get 22 in the month, but I still stand amazed.

Last night was fun. Elder Greener and I slept in the President’s office. I’m really getting along well with Elder Greener. I’m thankful for that. Another miracle that happened is that we planned a shindig to get Marcelo and Fernanda married, because he received an answer that the Book of Mormon is true. It was sweet – we got with Irmão Alex and cooked Strogonoff and set up a dinner for 2 in the church. Sam bought rings for them and we left them alone so Marcelo could pop the question. It was great. Everyone was crying – it’s amazing to see the Gospel blessing families. I know it’s true. I pray that I can always live worthy of this KNOWLEDGE that I have.

Another cool thing that has happened is that as a District Leader I had my first Baptismal Interview with a kid named Paulo. Fortunately it was way easy and he was ready. It was a good experience. I hope to be able to do many more!

Bruna has been hard to visit, but we’re still praying that we can mark her baptism for this week. Miracles are real! I’m happy working hard, and Elder Stucki and I are getting along well. I’m thankful for all I’ve been given.

body: Wow! Yesterday we had an experience that was really special. We were at João’s house, but he was working on his car outside. So, our lesson that we had prepared for the whole family was postponed, and we just followed our impressions and started to teach about the Gift of the Holy Ghost. After bearing testimony a bit, João entered and sat with us. I decided to ask about the Word of Wisdom and if they were liking the Cevada. Fátima said she was trying to adjust, laughingly. This is when the Spirit entered the room: João looked at her and said, “Look, when Lehi was in the wilderness the Lord blessed their raw meat to be sweet so they could survive and be blessed following Him!” I looked at Elder Barbosa in awe. We testified that THIS is how the Holy Ghost works. That if they had dúvidas, this was the answer to their prayers! We all recognized the Spirit together. The Book of Mormon is incredible. The power it has to inspire the mind and teach principles is divine. João also is reading Gospel Principles and gained a testimony about the Sacrament. Today I want to talk a bit more about the ordinance and explain the prayers. I pray that the Lord works a mighty MIRACLE in the house. This truly was an unforgettable experience. I’m grateful that the Lord strengthens my weaknesses and gives me Grace in His hands. Amen.

body: Today was a kinda hard day... We had lunch with Bishop Wagner and we spoke alot about José Ometto and how it needs a group there so the families can go to church. I felt really good about this goal, especially after feeling that we should work there... I decided to call President Castro Deus to ask him about it. He didn’t think it was a good idea and told us not to work far from the Chapel. I was confused, but knowing that he has the keys, we turned around and won’t work there more, just with the few referrals that we have. I don’t know why we felt so strong to work there if this was gonna happen, but I know that God will recompense our obedience. I have alot of hope in this. Elder Barbosa and I discussed alot on this subject and we will talk to President Tanner about this in July – because maybe this idea is preparatory. But, in other news, we had Conselho da Ala today, and we established plans to put Elder Perry’s ward mission plan in full effect. I’m pretty excited about this. It appears that the Baptism of João and Fátima and Natália really has got the ward excited. By small and simple things.

title: Journal entry
body: Yesterday was a bit of a crazy day – I needed to go to Cosmópolis to do an interview. A member told us that in the Trevo de Jaguariúna there is a bus stop that has a bus that goes to Cosmópolis. So, we went there 2:30 and waited, and waited... and waited. Turns out, there isn’t a bus that goes straight to Cosmópolis, haha. We had to take the bus to Artur Nogueira and then go to Cosmópolis. It was 7:00 when we finally arrived. It would have been impossible to get a bus home, but a member in Cosmópolis helped us out with a ride. So, it all worked out in the end! Today was a hard day – almost everything fell through. But we taught Michele, we read some of the Book of Mormon together. She really has potential. I pray that we can help her truly commit herself to the Gospel. Silene also seems super elect. We passed by her house and spoke w/ her for a few minutes. She read the BoM and said she really liked it. Let’s see where we get with her! I think she’s a baptism – just have to marry her first. Good times.

title: Journal entry
body: Today I had some good experiences. This morning Sister Yokoyama called really upset. She was crying. She was upset because Sister Barros was depressed – and in bad health – and had called President because she felt that she needed to go home. I listened. And I felt the Spirit guide me. I opened Preach my Gospel to the Atonement in the 2nd lesson, that mentions how it can cure us from our pains and sadness, and how everything can be corrected through the Atonement. I asked her if she believed in this promise, and if she believed that this promise is valid for Sister Barros too. She said yes and said she felt Him with her. I later spoke with Sister Barros and I think I was able to help lift her spirits a bit, at least we had a few laughs. Today we also taught the family of Marcia, Letícia, Beatriz, Vitor. They are an inactive family, and their kids aren’t baptized. We left a first lesson and I really felt the Spirit alot. We were guided. I really felt that the Lord needs them for something. I also felt that they are ready to come back. I’m really grateful that the Lord is leading my work. Worthiness is key to recognizing and following the Spirit.

title: Journal entry
body: This week has flown by – and we’ve had a few miracles in the interim. Looks like Pamela will be baptized this week – we’re pretty stoked for her. We’re also helping Michele and Tatiana so they can be baptized too. Today we taught the Word of Wisdom for Michele and, although she has been drinking and stuff with her friends, she accepted to stop and live the commandment – which was awesome. I was expecting a “well, I’ll try...” kind of response, but she committed w/o hesitation. We also taught a powerful lesson with Tatiana today about the Atonement – and then we went to Wilson, Leila and Yuri’s house. What great family! We’re gonna help them come back to church and baptize Yuri on the 8th. It seems like they already have the desire to come back – which is good. I know the Church is true and that the Gift of the Holy Ghost is real and that the Priesthood is true, divine power. I love being worthy. I love the Peace of the Spirit. I love receiving revelation. Sister Barros called tonight, sad. She’s passing through some tough times, but I feel that I was able to help her a bit – I felt the Spirit working. What a gift! I feel myself growing and becoming a better person – this is an answer to my prayers.

title: Journal entry
body: Our lessons with Michele and Tatiana fell through today – but we managed to teach Pamela. She’s a bit apprehensive about her baptism, but we’re praying and she is too, that everything will work out. I’m grateful to be here on the mission. I love serving others, and teaching, and using and developing my gifts. It really is through service that our gifts grow with divine aid. I feel it. I’m starting to feel more and more the blessing I received to have the “capacity to do good in the lives of others.” What a blessing! In the end, it all comes down to the good that we do for others. This is what lasts. This is what is Eternal and Celestial. I feel Christ’s presence as I worry about others – I’m starting to recognize His love more fully. I know the Gospel is true.

title: Journal entry
body: We had Pamela’s baptism today! It went well. Her mom and her grandma were there, too. I felt really good today in the fast and testimony meeting. I was really touched. I’m really feeling the Spirit in my life – an inner peace and a constant burning. I love it so much. Life is so much better like this. When we sin we truly are left to ourselves and the Spirit withdraws – and realizing just how good it is to commune with Him like this really does remove temptation from me. It helps me. If we can just choose to start living the principles, life is so much better and happier! This week we’re gonna focus on Tatiana and Yuri. I’m really liking the members here in Jaguariúna. I’ll be sad to be transferred from here. This transfer is passing really fast – I’m glad that we’re enjoying the work and are getting lost in it.

title: Journal entry
body: This last week passed by really fast. Alot happened. We visited Wilson, Leila and Yuri alot this week – because it was possible that he could be baptized. I really like that family. I feel good with them. Friday we had a division to do baptismal interviews. Elder Standage came here to Jaguariúna and I went to Cosmópolis with Elder Macedo. But something crazy happened. When I woke up that day – as I was brushing my teeth, the vinear on my front tooth broke loose! Oh man is it hideous without that thing! So I had to rush and try to find a Dentist that would accept me without an appointment, which proved difficult. I ended up marking an emergency appointment in Cosmópolis – actually I had Sister Yokoyama mark it for me haha. It all turned out well in the end. Irmão Wilson said that he would travel, so it seemed that Yuri’s baptism had fallen through, but we were OK – because it’s important that the Dad is there at the baptism. Saturday was an interesting day – Irmã Fabiana came to Jaguariúna to visit one of her aunts with us. She took forever and we pretty much wasted the whole day waiting for her, but it all worked out! It was good to see her. Then Sunday – Irmão Wilson showed up at church! So we talked with him and he said that he wouldn’t leave until tomorrow! So we remarked Yuri’s baptism – and that’s how the miracle happened. Yay! The mission is great!

body: This last week passed by slowly, and I felt a bit lost in the area. But we still had some really good moments. We found a woman named Claudia, she’s a referral from Irmão Antonio. And she’s showing a lot of interest in our message. I’m excited about teaching her. This week has started out pretty well. I like doing missionary work, I like talking to people and inviting people. Few understand the importance, but I believe that many, many seeds are being planted. I’d like to think that each contact is a seed that a future missionary will reap. I’ll never know the full outcome of my mission – nobody does. But I like the idea that I have the opportunity to influence lives. Members, non-members alike. What a blessing. Our gifts are important.

body: This week has been great! We had a week long training with all the leaders in the mission. It’s a new training that focuses on the Doctrine of Christ, Love, the invitations to read, pray, and go to church, and revelation, among other things. It was great – these new insights will really help the work all over the world. I can feel that it’s better – it’s all focused on PEOPLE, not lessons. It’s more Christ like. I was in divisions this whole week with Elder Bavender. We arrived together (even though he was in the other CTM district). I like him alot! We get along really well. It was fun. I would have liked to have been able to teach with him. Maybe in the future – who knows!

title: Journal entry
body: Monday I received a call – I’ve been transferred! Crazy, I wasn’t expecting this. I’ve been called to be a Zone Leader! I’m now working in Americana with Elder Swenson – who arrived with me here in Brazil. I feel good about this calling and I pray that I will have the ability to use my talents to help these Elders and this Stake grow. I had an interview w/ Elder Gabriel (assistente) and it was really good. He told me about how he was there when I was called and that I truly was called of God. The other day when I was praying, I received my confirmation that I was truly called for this calling – a frase from my Patriarcal Blessing popped into my head: “I bless you w/ the capacity and ability to grow and develop in your love for others and in your ability to meet their needs, and to sense in your heart how to accomplish the service in their behalf that needs to be performed.” I know that this is my mission here. I’m grateful for revelation.

title: Journal entry
body:
This past week has been really good. One good thing that happened was a division with Elder Aste. I got to show him the new trainings and we had an amazing lesson with a woman named Cidinha. We read the Book of Mormon in 1st Nephi and explained Ch 12–14 about apostasy and the role of the Book of Mormon. As I was baring my testimony I felt the Spirit really strong and I told her “We’re feeling Him now!” She closed her eyes and a sublime look came over her face. We sat in silence for a few moments. It was really powerful. The power of the Holy Ghost truly is what converts.

A few days after this, Elder Swenson and I were walking and a woman called our name and asked for the name of the Bishop – turns out she’s a member of another ward. We chit chat a bit and I ask her if she knows someone nearby that we can visit. She says yes! and takes us to the house of a woman named Mara. Mara is living in a tough situation, her son is using drugs and has kicked her to the fundos. She doesn’t have much, and she takes care of 2 grandkids and a daughter. But she has a heart of Gold and a lot of Faith. We’re teaching her and she’s getting ready for baptism. We’re excited and know that God will be able to bless her life even more in the true Gospel.

I’m liking Carioba alot, and it’s good to work w/ Elder Swenson. He’s a hard worker with a lot of purity. He’s a good example to me. I’m working to overcome my weaknesses – I truly need God’s help. I feel so weak at times. But I believe in the Atonement and know that I can become who I want to be. I just need to have patience with myself and truly TRY to correct myself.

Worthyness and personal effort are so important to have the Spirit with us.

Without the Spirit, life just isn’t that satisfying.

title: Journal entry
body:
Yesterday was a day of Miracles! It’s interesting that on the mission so many miracles happen that we sometimes get desensitized. I’m sure there are many miracles that I have forgotten to write here – and that makes me sad.

But yesterday we followed up with Mara and Carol. Carol said she prayed and asked God if the Church is true and she dreamed that Christ appeared to her, with open arms, and told her it is. Wow. What a blessing!

We also had a lesson with Cieldo – Gisele’s uncle. He’s about 25 years old. He’s never frequented a certain religion, but has a strong faith. He responded really well to the restoration and accepted baptism firmly! It was funny, because he said “now you guys just have to follow up with me and help me prepare!” haha! Super-elect!

We’re really excited and grateful to see the hand of God so much – in spite of our weaknesses.

title: Journal entry
body:
I feel bad that it’s so hard for me to update my diary. So much has happened.

The most important thing is that yesterday Gisele was baptized! Yeah! It went really well! It was interesting because we kept waiting for the trial of faith but it never happened... everyone supported her decision. It was also a good experience because Antonio (a recent-convert) receive the Aaronic Priesthood and baptized her on the same day. It was a really good experience.

Each day I feel the importance of sharing our talents. Yesterday Elder Swenson and I played a special musical number in Sacrament meeting (Nearer My God to Thee). He played piano and I violin. Although simply everyone loved it and said they really felt the Spirit. What a blessing it is to have a talent that other people like. It feels good to share it.

Tomorrow is transfers already. Wow it passed by fast. I feel we really have been working hard. I’m getting the hang of being a Zone Leader. We just have to be a good example. And worry about the wellbeing of the other Elders. It’s a blessing to serve.

I had an interesting experience the other day too, that I’ll write in my other journal.

title: Journal entry
body:
This week has been good. We had an interview and a training with President Tanner. He passed us his vision of the mission as a contacting mission. We had a wonderful experience when we got together in our Zone to pass this information to our Elders. It was a good experience because they all got excited. I truly saw how we as Zone Leaders have a power to truly motivate and inspire. This gave me a confidence that I can help the Zone grow; I CAN make a difference. I thank God for this experience.

We’ve been focusing a lot on Alessandro and Mara these weeks. Alessandro has almost stopped smoking – but he’s have trouble committing to the final step.

Mara seems a little hesitant for baptism, but I believe that she really needs the Gift of Holy Ghost to protect her and help her avoid the dangers that surround her. We really need to help her understand this.

I’m really excited about this Month – I feel that a lot of miracles will happen in our Zone.

title: Journal entry
body:
Wow – time has flown. These past couple of weeks have been interesting. I feel good about the amount of work we’ve done. The Zone has improved alot in its contacts. But unfortunately we’ve haven’t seen many fruits. Or rather any fruits. Elder Swenson and I have had the hardest time getting our investigators to church. They say they’ll go and then they all fall through! It’s been frustrating because we get really excited when they say they’ll go and then it makes us really sad when they don’t.

Our game plan is to just keep finding new investigators until we find the ones that are willing to assume the invitation and keep their commitments. I know the fruits will come. An important principle is that “success as a missionary is determined by our DEDICATION” (PMG – cap 1). There is solace in this.

I find my self in a constant state of awe in relation to TIME. It’s so hard to believe that so much time has passed since I got here on the mission. Wow....

I love seeing how everything seems to fall into place when you’re working hard.

We went out with Paulo yesterday. He said it was the first time missionaries had invited him. He said he wants to serve a mission. I am so happy to hear that! I feel like we can make an impact on his desire to serve. I’m glad that God inspired us to invite him to do divisions with us.

title: Happy Halloween!
body:
Happy Halloween!

Two good things happened today:

First, Alessandro went to church!

Second, we went to Praia Azul for lunch. On the Bus I did a contact with a man that went to church and met w/ the Elders for 6 months in 2002. Valdemar is his name. We took his address and went straight to his house after lunch. He is going through depression as a withdrawal of bebidas – it has been one month since he’s stopped. We marked his baptism and gave him a blessing. I know that God placed him in our path, for many, many small factors and decisions led us to cross paths. God truly guides us.

body:
We had some good lessons today. We taught William’s family. His wife and daughter are pretty Catholic, but I think we’ll get to them through William. He’s showing alot of interest. We’re really excited.

Gisele, too. Wow she’s really looking for an answer. She has a lot of doubts and questions. It’s this type of “pondering” that’s gonna lead her to an answer. I hope I’m here to see these investigators receive their answers.

We decided, after prayer, and in spite of the time, to catch a bus to Praia Azul to teach Valdemar. It was cool, because two days ago I talked to President Tanner about teaching lessons on the street. I did a contact and the man asked us what we preach. So I taught him the first lesson in 2 minutes. It felt really good to teach a mini lesson like that. I’m gonna do it way more. I think it’ll make a big difference in my mission.

We got to Valdemar’s house really late and he didn’t want to let us in, so we taught him at the Portão. It was good that we went by. We taught the law of Chastity and gave him a “Finding Faith in Christ” DVD.

We got home late. But it was a really good day and I’m feeling really good about the quality of our investigators. It’s so much better when we just pray and let God lead us to His elect and prepared.

So today was a hectic day – but a blessed day.

Elder Stone was with us and we did Erick’s baptismal interview in the morning for his baptism today at 7 PM.

It went well – all smooth... And then after lunch we went to fill the Baptismal “Pool” in the chapel. It didn’t fill up right and gave us hours of trouble trying to keep it level as it filled. There were 5 of us involved in the project: me, Elder Pietz, Vander, Johan, and Flávio. haha. But it all worked out.

SO... at 6:30 ish I was in division w/ Johan and we went to get Erick. Well, he wasn’t at his house.

We waited a bit and thought maybe he went to the chapel by himself. We got to the chapel at 7 and he wasn’t there, BUT, everyone was there waiting. Ah! haha.

So, I grabbed Flávio and we headed out again. What was nice is that I was calm the whole time. I kept a confidence in the Lord that it would work out somehow. I told Flávio that “we have to have faith even until the last moment!” We went to his grandma’s house; he wasn’t there. We went back to his house – and on the way I felt I should stop and ask some kids in the street if they knew him. They said they knew him but hadn’t seen him. We got back to his house and he still wasn’t there.

So, I just sat down in front of his house, prayed a little more, and waited. Within a few minutes he showed up – walking down the street! We talked to him and he said he wasn’t really wanting to get baptized any more. We went and talked to his mom and she was a little reluctant too – just because of his indecision.

I just stepped back and looked at the situation like “Is this really happening?” and laughed.

I gave a “LIÇÃO DE FÉ” and thru the Spirit we got him back on board.

I called Vander and told him we were coming.

We got to the chapel at 8 and the baptism happened.

I endured to the last minute and followed the Spirit in the process and the Lord showed His mighty hand.

What had happened is that the kids in the street that I was inspired to talk to had found him and sent him over to us. How cool to see the Spirit work thru a simple thought. Had I of not followed the idea, the baptism might not of even happened!

So... I’m on the plane... Going home... I thought I’d reflect a bit...

The mission has taught me a lot. It has taught me to completely trust in God. Truly, everything works out when we trust His will.

I received powerful confirmations that the church is true and that the Priesthood has truly been restored; Joseph really was a Prophet.

I learned the importance of worthiness.

I learned the importance of friendships.
